key_insight: Greater night-to-night sleep variability was associated with prolonged post-enrollment hospitalization in acute psychiatric inpatients.
clinical_relevance: Sleep variability from wearables or routine nursing observations may offer a practical marker of longer hospitalization, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Prospective observational study of 94 acute psychiatric inpatients.
Sleep variability measured as each patient's standard deviation of nightly total sleep time across 5–7 available observations.
Age- and sex-adjusted models assessed post-enrollment stays longer than 24 days.
evidence_signal: Among 94 patients, 23 had prolonged stays; each 1-hour increase in actigraphy-derived sleep variability was associated with adjusted odds of 2.30 (95% CI 1.08–4.93), with model AUC 0.756 versus 0.692 for age and sex alone.
watch_item: This small, single-unit observational study does not establish causality; monitoring began after enrollment and often covered nonconsecutive nights.
paper_title: Sleep Variability From Routine Nursing Observation and Wearable Actigraphy and Post-Enrollment Length of Stay in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients: Prospective Observational Study
